title: VLAN tag (802.1Q)
summary: An 802.1Q VLAN tag is a 4-byte field inserted into an Ethernet frame between the source MAC and the EtherType. Fields: TPID (Tag Protocol Identifier, 2 bytes, 0x8100), PCP (Priority Code Point, 3 bits, 0-7), DEI (Drop Eligible Indicator, 1 bit), VID (VLAN Identifier, 12 bits, 1-4094).

ext.summary: An 802.1Q VLAN tag is a 4-byte field inserted into an Ethernet frame between the source MAC and the EtherType. Fields: TPID (Tag Protocol Identifier, 2 bytes, 0x8100), PCP (Priority Code Point, 3 bits, 0-7), DEI (Drop Eligible Indicator, 1 bit), VID (VLAN Identifier, 12 bits, 1-4094).

structure.meaning: Tag Protocol Identifier: 0x8100 (802.1Q). Other values: 0x88A8 (QinQ outer), 0x9100 (legacy QinQ).
Priority Code Point: 0 (best effort) to 7 (highest). Maps to 802.1p priority.
Drop Eligible Indicator: 1 = frame may be dropped under congestion.
VLAN Identifier: 1-4094 (0 and 4095 are reserved). 4094 possible VLANs.

ext.example_decoded: VLAN tag: TPID 0x8100, PCP 0, DEI 0, VID 1
notes: VLAN tags enable virtual LANs (network segmentation).
QinQ (802.1ad) uses double tagging (outer + inner) for provider networks.
VLANs are used for network isolation, QoS, and multi-tenancy.
The VID 0 is reserved (priority-tagged frame). VID 4095 is reserved.
802.1Q is the standard for VLAN tagging.
